title: A2 Week 01 — Requests ladder: Please vs Can vs Could vs Would (interactive)

items.prompt: External email (vendor). Choose the most polite request.
options: Can you send the updated invoice?
Could you please send the updated invoice?
items.explanation: External emails often use Could/Would for a more professional tone.

items.prompt: Internal email (teammate). Choose the best request (clear, not too formal).
options: Would you be able to send the file at your earliest convenience?
Can you send the file today?
items.explanation: Internal: Can you…? is neutral and clear.

options: Could you to send the file?
items.explanation: Correct pattern: Could you + base verb.

items.prompt: Choose the best request to confirm receipt (external).
items.explanation: Use base verb “confirm”. Could you… is more polite for external.

items.instructions: Complete with: send / confirm / check / resend
items.text:
1) Could you ____ the updated file?
2) Please ____ receipt.
3) Can you ____ page 2?
4) Would you ____ the link, please?
items.explanation: Base verb after Can/Could/Would; Please + base verb.

items.instructions: Complete with: by / on / at / to
items.text:
1) Please send it ____ Friday.
2) Can we meet ____ Tuesday?
3) The call is ____ 10:00.
4) Could you reply ____ EOD?
items.explanation: by + deadline, on + day/date, at + time.

items.instructions: Put the requests from more direct → more polite.
items.explanation: Typical ladder: Please → Can → Could → Would.

items.instructions: Put the steps in the correct order (instructions).

pairs.explanation: After Would you, use base verb: confirm.

pairs.wrong: First, please to check the file.

pairs.explanation: Use Could you… for a polite question; avoid mixed punctuation.
